purpose: Test whether frozen-base retention helps a short LoRA adaptation preserve recognised critical spans while gaining drug names.

matching.initialisation: zero-effect LoRA on the same locked Whisper Turbo base
matching.roles: Same locked PxCorpus export and train-only examples, shared seed and ordering.

windows_in_order.role: Historical descriptive comparison; known difficult cases.
Additional development clips, same eight voices; not an independent holdout.

generation.grid_freeze: Before any free generation in this experiment, bind both critical grids to selected reference SHA-256 and freeze the scoring code.
generation.reserved_benchmark_85: Do not score or inspect this reserve to tune either treatment. Use an independently prepared confirmation set for any subsequent adoption.

gate_each_window: No introduced failure for any scored medication, dose, fraction, decimal, sign, unit, negation, duration, numbers or association; record unmeasured categories and audit regression cases.
All clips terminate with the end token.
Cumulative and median generation time each at most 110 percent of the paired base; timings are exploratory on MPS.
gate_additional64: Fewer total word edits than the paired base.
At least one correctly recognised drug-name gain and no loss of a drug known to the paired base.
decision.paired_base_disagreement: Report per-clip baseline differences; if nonzero, make no causal comparison of arm differences without an independent replay.
decision.tie_and_failure: If neither passes retain the shipped model. If both pass report both treatments; favour simpler CE unless KL gives a clear critical gain. No threshold, weight, seed, validation window or checkpoints chosen after seeing results.
decision.limit: A pass is eligible only for a separate exported and quantised comparison on new voices; neither merge nor export runs here.
